rationale: The two "certifications" (MA(oancf/at) and NEG(MA((ib−oancf)/at))) are both monotone increasing in operating cash flow and therefore highly correlated, so MIN of their ranks will largely reproduce either archived signal (both already ~4.7% alpha) rather than test genuine complementarity — a near-cosmetic recombination of two existing results.

Research efficiency (ib per dollar of accumulated R&D) is a certification leg the archive has not tried, but note the mechanical tension that the yield leg is decreasing in R&D stock while the commitment leg is increasing in R&D intensity, so partial cancellation and heavy clustering of non-reporters at zero are real risks.

The expression and expected negative sign are internally consistent and the design sensibly conjoins the archive's strongest short-side slope with its strongest short-side alpha, but with re/at and oancf/lt as the two ingredients it risks collapsing into a generic financial-distress composite (a well-documented anomaly) rather than a purchase-accounting-specific effect.

This addresses a genuine open design question (within-firm versus cross-sectional measurement of research commitment) with a construction fix that removes the degenerate TS_MAX denominator that crippled the earlier 4% coverage variant, though TS_RANK over five annual observations is coarse and degenerate for non-R&D firms.

Economically coherent and the ib-based restatement plausibly lifts coverage above the oancf-constrained leader, but it is the third conjunction built on the same commitment-floor leg and the restated-profitability leg itself embeds R&D intensity, so incremental information over existing family members may be small.

This is a single-input numerator swap (oancf → ib) on an already-tested validation ratio family, and cross-sectional variation in the ratio is likely dominated by the inverse of intangible intensity in the denominator, so the coverage gain does not clearly justify it as a substantively different test.
